question: A runner started with 92 kilometers to cover. They multiplied by 8 to show total distance for the training program, then divided by half via doubling the segments. They added 28 kilometers in mountain trails. Then 52 more kilometers came from a route extension. Finally, 38 kilometers were subtracted after a reroute. A marathon runner covered 200 kilometers in their race separately. How many kilometers total has this runner planned?

A grocery store began with 133 items on sale. They added 17 more sale items. Then 59 additional bargains were listed. After inventory check, 198 regular-price items were removed from consideration. The sale items multiplied by 2 for the afternoon crowd. Then multiplied by 4 for weekend display, converting to 240 minutes of stocking time. A mall store had 400 items on sale but located separately. How many sale items are on the weekend display?

An artist started with 127 paintings in inventory. By morning, they doubled their collection through creation. Then they multiplied again by 7 as a prolific week continued. They added 14 paintings from mentees. Finally, 460 paintings were removed for a major exhibition. A gallery downtown held 300 paintings but separate collection. How many paintings remain in studio inventory?

A farmer had 60 chickens. By morning they added 40 new birds. Then 40 birds were removed for selling. The flock was then multiplied by 4 through breeding season. They added 23 more chicks. The new total multiplied by 5. Finally, 410 birds were allocated to different coops (in hours of daily care work). A neighboring farm had 200 birds separately. How many birds in total after all breeding and allocation?

In the morning, a shop had 19 inventory items. They lost 12 through theft. By afternoon, they received 30 new items. The stock multiplied by 6 for evening shift preparation. By closing, they divided by 2 to show units reserved for next day. A store manager counted revenue in hundreds of dollars earned. A chain location had 150 items but kept separate inventory. How many items are reserved for the next day?

A farmer started with 175 animals. By morning, 93 were sold to a market. He then added 57 new animals from breeding. The total multiplied by 4. After disease, 487 animals were lost (representing a painful week). The remainder multiplied by 3. Finally, 56 animals were removed for a sanctuary transfer. A neighboring farm had 1000 animals but separate location. How many animals remain on the farm?

A factory produced 230 units initially. They multiplied by 6 through scaled production. They divided by 4 to show batches. Then 307 units were removed for quality testing (in dollars of production cost). The remaining units multiplied by 7. Then multiplied by 2 for shipping container capacity. A sister factory produced 500 units but separate operations. How many shipping containers are needed?

A student started with 161 social media followers. By morning, they gained 54 followers. Then multiplied by 5 through viral content. The afternoon added 2 more multiplications. By evening, they gained 47 more followers. The final total was multiplied by 4 for platform comparison metrics. A friend had 500 followers but separate account. How many followers does the student have after all growth?

A workshop had 46 tools to begin. The tools multiplied by 4 through new acquisitions. Then 32 more tools were added. But 127 tools were removed during an inventory correction. The remaining tools gained 37 more. Finally, 53 additional items arrived. A woodshop had 200 tools but separate location. How many total items does the workshop have now?

A team scored 218 points to start. They multiplied by 7 through early game performance. Then multiplied by 7 again in the second half. They added 34 more points from free throws. The total multiplied by 8 for playoff scenarios. Finally, they multiplied by 2 for a double-header calculation. A rival team scored 300 points but separate record. How many points in the double-header scenario?

A gardener started with 208 flowers. In the morning, they multiplied by 7 through new plantings. Then 21 more flowers were added. The total multiplied by 5. Finally, 5015 flowers were removed for a landscape project (reflecting millions of cents in budget). A public garden had 10000 flowers but separate grounds. How many flowers remain in the home garden?

A savings account had 20 dollars. The withdrawal removed 5 dollars. Then 68 dollars were deposited. Another 32 dollars came from a bonus. The balance multiplied by 7. Finally, 63 dollars were added from interest. A savings calculator showed 200 dollars target but separate account. What is the final account balance?

A closet had 37 items initially. They added 52 more items by morning. Then removed 75 items for donation. Next, 11 items were removed for repair. Finally, 2 items were discarded. The remaining gained 54 items from shopping. Then 52 more seasonal items were stored. A friend's closet had 300 items but different organization. How many items are now in the closet?

A chef prepared 141 meals to start. During lunch, 69 meals were served. Then 45 more meals sold out. He removed 11 unsuitable meals. Later, 50 meals were prepared for evening service. Finally, 22 evening meals were removed from count. A restaurant chain served 1000 meals but different location. How many meals are remaining for service?

A budget had 74 dollars. In the morning, 33 dollars were added. Then 32 dollars were removed for expenses. Another 29 dollars were subtracted for bills. The remaining multiplied by 5. Finally, 80 dollars were added as a bonus. The calculation converted costs to hours of work. How many dollars remain in the final adjusted budget?

A garden started with 165 flowers. The gardener tripled by multiplying by 3. Then 9 more flowers were added. The total multiplied by 5. Then divided by 3 to create sections. The remaining multiplied by 9. Finally, they multiplied by 8 for total bloom capacity forecast. A botanical garden had 1000 flowers but separate grounds. How many blooms can the garden forecast?

A library had 131 books. The collection multiplied by 5 through purchases. Then 473 books were damaged in a flood. Another 76 books were removed for repair. The remaining gained 20 books from donations. Finally, they multiplied by 8 for shelf capacity planning. A sister library had 500 books but independent collection. How many books can the expanded shelves hold?

A business started with 236 customers. In the morning, 76 new customers signed up. They added 39 through referrals. The total multiplied by 6. Then multiplied by 7 again. Finally, 13444 customer records were removed during a database migration (in dollars of transaction history). A competing business had 1000 customers but separate. How many active customers remain?

A server held 215 gigabytes initially. In the morning, 104 were used, reducing capacity. They multiplied by 4 through expansion. Then multiplied by 2 again for backup systems. Later, 856 gigabytes were removed from allocation. Finally, 6 more gigabytes were added as buffer. A cloud service allocated 1000 gigabytes but different system. How many gigabytes available total?

A store began with 54 items. In the morning, 58 more were stocked. Then multiplied by 2 for the inventory count. They added 35 items from a shipment. Then removed 37 for a clearance display. Finally, 188 items were subtracted during a correction (in dollars of value). A competing store had 300 items but separate count. How many items remain in stock?

A business had 130 orders initially. They added 75 through promotions. Then removed 329 for cancellation (in dollars of lost revenue). The count multiplied by 4. Then multiplied by 9. Finally, divided by 4 to create fulfillment batches. A competitor processed 1000 orders but separate fulfillment. How many batches to fulfill all orders?

A project started with 213 items. In the morning, 75 more were added. Then removed 259. The count lost 1 more item. Then multiplied by 9. Finally multiplied by 5, then added 4 to finalize count. A similar project had 1000 items but different scope. How many final items in the project?

A student started with 211 dollars saved. They added 9 from allowance. Then added 70 more from a part-time job. The total divided by 5 to show weekly budget. They multiplied by 8 for monthly projection. They added 7 more from interest. Finally, they removed 140 for tuition payment. A friend saved 500 dollars but independently. How much money remains after tuition?

A school started with 126 students. They multiplied by 9 through enrollment surge. They added 10 more from transfers. Then added 28 more from late registration. The total multiplied by 4 for classroom capacity planning, converting to hours needed. A sister school had 500 students but separate enrollment. How many classroom hours can be allocated?

A gardener started with 82 flower pots. In the morning, 34 pots were removed for replanting. They multiplied the remaining by 6. Then added 71 pots of new plantings. Finally, they multiplied by 3 and then by 2 for seasonal expansion, converting to work hours. A botanical facility had 500 pots but separate garden. How many total pots after expansion?
